name: Fergus
tagline: Job management for trade businesses: quoting, scheduling, timesheets, and invoicing for plumbers, electricians, and similar crews.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not exotic: customers, sites, jobs, quotes with line items, time entries, invoices. An agent can produce a local job tracker that quotes, schedules, and invoices for a one-person operation in a weekend, and it will feel faster than the real thing because it has none of the settings. What breaks is everything that leaves your laptop: the phone app your crew actually uses on a roof with no signal, the accounting sync that stops you double-entering every invoice, and the supplier price files that make quoting fast instead of guesswork. If you are solo, bill a handful of jobs a month, and already do your own bookkeeping, the DIY version is genuinely viable. If you have three vans and a bookkeeper, you are rebuilding an ERP by accident.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you create customers and jobs, build quotes from a reusable rate and materials list, log time against jobs, then turn accepted quotes and logged time into printable invoices you can chase.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine you can leave running, or a small VPS
Your own materials and labour rates entered once as seed data
A way to send PDFs (browser print to PDF plus your normal email is enough)
Manual re-entry into whatever accounting software you file tax with
whatYouLose: A field-ready mobile app with offline capture, photos, and signatures
Two-way sync with Xero or MYOB, so every invoice gets keyed in twice
Supplier price catalogs and margin defaults that make quoting fast
A scheduling board that handles multiple techs, travel, and recurring maintenance
Backups, audit trail, and someone to call when the invoice numbering goes weird
moatNotes: The accounting sync is the real lock-in. Once a year of invoices and GST lives in the pipe between Fergus and Xero, leaving is a data migration, not a decision.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because trade businesses are not paying for a job list, they are paying to not chase paperwork at 9pm. The value is the mobile app the apprentice will actually open, the invoice that lands the same day the job finishes, and the accounting integration that means the numbers you quoted are the numbers your bookkeeper sees. A self-built tracker replaces the database and none of the discipline. It also gives you a new unpaid job: maintaining it during your actual busy season.
notes: Fine as a solo-operator quoting and invoicing tool, hopeless the moment a second person needs it on a phone.
prompt:
Build a local-first job management app for a one-person trade business. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Zod for validation. Single process, run with npm run dev. Store the database file at ./data/app.db and create it on first boot with migrations run in code.

Data model:
- customers: name, phone, email, billing address, notes
- sites: belongs to a customer, address, access notes
- jobs: customer, site, title, description, status (enquiry, quoted, accepted, in_progress, complete, invoiced, paid), scheduled_date, created_at
- rate_items: reusable labour and materials lines with code, description, unit, cost, sell price
- quote_lines: belongs to a job, description, qty, unit, sell price, optional rate_item link
- time_entries: job, date, hours, description, hourly rate
- invoices: job, number, issue date, due date, status, snapshot of lines as JSON so later edits never mutate a sent invoice

Screens:
1. Job board: columns by status, drag or dropdown to move a job, quick add.
2. Job detail: customer and site, quote builder that autocompletes from rate_items and shows subtotal, tax, total, time entry logging, and a button to generate an invoice from accepted quote lines plus unbilled time.
3. Rate items CRUD, with CSV import so a supplier price list can be pasted in.
4. Invoices list with overdue highlighting, and a print-friendly invoice page styled for browser print to PDF.
5. Simple dashboard: value quoted this month, value invoiced, unpaid total.

Rules: tax rate and business details (name, address, tax number, invoice number prefix) live in .env and are rendered on invoices. Invoice numbers are sequential and never reused. Money in integer cents, never floats. Every mutation is a server action with Zod validation.

Out of scope, do not build: multi-user auth, mobile app, email sending, accounting integrations, payment processing, GPS or route planning.

Include a seed script with two customers, ten rate items, and three jobs in different statuses, plus a README with setup, backup instructions (copy data/app.db), and a one-paragraph honest note on what this does not replace.
